controls.name: begin-refused
controls.replace: Msg::Begin => (S { store: s.store, failed: true, tx: None }, Ans::Failure),
controls.classification: repair (alternative): BEGIN refused with FAILURE, as design Refuse; the client is told there is no transaction, so every as-built departure theorem and the commit neighbor change

controls.name: atomic-tx
controls.classification: repair (intended): BEGIN opens a transaction whose writes are held until COMMIT; ROLLBACK, RESET and a closed connection discard them

controls.name: rollback-answers-failure
controls.classification: answer: ROLLBACK answered FAILURE instead of SUCCESS (the client would learn the writes stayed)

controls.name: run-not-committed
controls.classification: decision: a successful RUN's write not committed by execute_cypher (removes P-AUTOCOMMIT); the auto-commit neighbor and every theorem built on the lemma lose their store

controls.name: failed-run-writes
controls.classification: premise P-STMT-ATOMIC flipped: a failing statement keeps its own writes

controls.name: failure-not-sticky
controls.classification: decision: the FAILED state's guard removed, so PULL and ROLLBACK after a failure are no longer IGNORED

controls.name: rule-rollback-keeps
controls.find: Msg::Rollback => C { store: c.store, tx: None, failed: false },
controls.replace: Msg::Rollback => match c.tx { Some(p) => C { store: c.store + p, tx: None, failed: false }, None => c },
controls.classification: rule weakened: the client ledger keeps a rolled-back transaction's writes (checks that the departure theorems constrain the rule, not only the server)
